doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Memorizing music and losing his stand on the first show
summary: Gibbs plays vibes from memory but on his first TV show stagehands took his music stand and he nearly missed a note.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I noticed that in the videos I’ve seen of you, you rarely have a music stand in front of the vibes.
Do you? Wow. And so when you wrote out parts for, let’s say your six piece band for Regis —
Then I would have the parts.
I’d have to have my part because you know I just wrote it and I didn’t even know what I wrote.

I’ll tell you my first show, I’ve got to tell you this. You know I’m coming from New York and I was still a jazz musician and I’m getting called to do a TV show, I didn’t know anything about playing jazz so in my contract it had to be written that I would perform three times a week on camera with my sextet. And so I’d be like an act, you know we’d have an act. And it got to be where I had so much to do that I didn’t want to do that. So the first show I took the tune I’d recorded and I had all the music for it that I wrote. So I had my music stand and we rehearsed, I had the music set in front of me. Came show time all of a sudden before the band could play the stage hands all came running over and they’re moving things and ripped off my take — took my stand away. I’ve got no music. What did I write? And luckily I remembered it but I missed one note because the most important thing to me is the ensemble you play at the beginning and at the end. And it’s a syndicated show so it’s not showing for two weeks later, and for two weeks I was having a nervous breakdown remembering, oh it’s going to come on the air that dumb note I played. You know it went by and I didn’t even know where that note was, when I saw the TV show. It went by so fast. I swear I’m listening — “where is that note I screwed up?” I didn’t even know where it was. And I couldn’t play it back. It was on the air.
